I listen for sounds that might mean someone is entering my home

I have lost my faith in people, life, or a higher power
I was betrayed by someone I trusted

vignette: Mark is a 32-year-old European American man who works as a combat pilot. He has been struggling with symptoms since he experienced a traumatic sexual assault several months ago. Mark’s life has been dramatically altered by the event, and he now finds himself constantly on edge, both inside his home and in public settings. The night of the trauma was a blur of fear and confusion for Mark. The perpetrator was someone he trusted deeply, which made the violation even more devastating. Since then, he often wakes up from nightmares drenched in sweat, still feeling the intensity of the moment. These dreams leave him with a lingering sense of unease that persists throughout his waking hours. Mark’s job as a combat pilot requires him to be vigilant and aware of potential threats constantly. However, since the assault, he has found it increasingly difficult to distinguish between real danger and perceived threats. He jumps or startles at ordinary sounds, such as the hum of an air conditioner or the creaking of floorboards. Inside his home, which should be a safe haven, Mark feels on guard, constantly listening for any signs that someone might have entered uninvited. This heightened sense of threat has been exacerbated by Mark’s negative appraisals about himself and others. He believes he is a lousy coper because of how he has reacted since the assault. His faith in people, life, and even a higher power has eroded, leaving him feeling betrayed and deeply mistrustful. These beliefs have made it challenging for Mark to feel safe or secure. His negative appraisals have led to an increase in his perception of threat. For instance, when he is at work, unpredictable situations trigger intense anxiety. The very unpredictability of combat scenarios now seems magnified, making him hyper-vigilant and often isolated from his colleagues. His fear that people are acting suspiciously has made it difficult for Mark to trust anyone, including those who have always been there for him. The cycle of negative appraisals and perceived threats has become a self-reinforcing loop. When he feels betrayed by someone he trusted, the sense of threat intensifies, leading him to overreact to even minor triggers. Conversely, these heightened feelings of threat reinforce his negative beliefs about himself and others, creating a vicious circle that is hard to break. Mark’s life has been significantly impacted by this cycle. He avoids social situations where unpredictability might be high, such as group gatherings or casual outings with friends. At work, he finds it increasingly difficult to collaborate effectively, often isolating himself from the team during missions out of fear and anxiety. This has led to strained relationships both personally and professionally. What finally brought Mark to seek help was a recent incident where his heightened state of alertness almost compromised a mission. He realized that if he did not address these issues soon, they would not only jeopardize his career but could also harm others around him. The most frightening part for Mark is the possibility of losing control and the fear of what this might mean about who he really is. Despite his fears, there is hope in seeing a therapist where he can process the trauma and work through these overwhelming feelings. He hopes that with support, he can regain some sense of trust and safety in his daily life and return to feeling like himself again.
